title: Springback in Tube Bending: How to Measure and Correct It
excerpt: Springback in tube bending, explained simply: why tube relaxes after a bend, how to find your number with a test bend, and how to overbend and log it.

notes: Direct page fetches were blocked in this environment (DNS/proxy), so every fact except the two writer-kit known-good facts (Rogue Fab 90 -> 86.5 deg; JD2 4130 ~2x mild steel) came from WebSearch result summaries, not a direct read. Re-check before publishing: (1) Kitplanes 'Home Shop Machinist' column: 7/8 x .049 4130 needed 98 deg to get 90 deg, and it repeats JD's 2x claim (search summary). (2) Artisan's Asylum makerspace wiki for its JD2 bender: springback 2-8 deg, found by trial and error, depends on bend angle and wall (secondary source, search summary). (3) The Fabricator 'Tube and pipe basics': harder tubes and smaller CLRs produce more springback and radial growth; stainless springs back more than steel (search summary). (4) Rogue Fab stainless page: stainless springs back more than mild steel and significantly more than aluminium; plan to overbend (search summary). (5) Advanced Tubular overbend calculator: two test bends, typically 20 and 120 deg (search summary). (6) NWPU TA18 titanium study: angular springback increases linearly with bend angle; angle and radius springback decrease with smaller radii; material property variation matters more than process parameters (abstract via search summary). (7) MATEC 2025 rotary-draw paper: larger die radius -> more radius recovery, less angle recovery (search summary). Items 3, 6 and 7 conflict on the effect of die radius; the article says so and does not pick a side. Left out as unverifiable: the Baileigh RDB-175 manual's '105 deg' calibration example from the fact-check notes (could not re-confirm), the Pro-Tools springback blog's 7 deg / 2 deg illustrations and its heat-number advice (page not reachable or surfaced), forum springback figures (anecdotal), and all sheet-metal springback figures. Amazon spec details for the Wixey WR365 (0.1 deg resolution, +/-0.2 deg accuracy, +/-180 deg range, flip-out backlit display, magnetic base) are from the Amazon listing as summarised by search; listings disagree on whether a battery is included, so the article says so. The two-point interpolation formula is plain linear interpolation, shown with letters only (no invented numbers).
